brief.verdict:
Not yet, but it can be, and the fixes are cheap. The nine current ads get the hardest part right. They use real app screens, and none is AI made in the way Justin fears. They will not beat the competitors yet, for five reasons that all three agents found independently.

1. Wrong moments for the audience. Ad 01 shows a Shaper (13 to 15) teenager script to parents of 8 to 13s. No ad covers the most intense problems for this age: mid match gaming rage, Snapchat pressure, the class group chat and the phone at night.
2. The hook is cut in half. "Three questions, no sign up." appears word for word on only 2 of 9 cards, and where it does, it is the smallest text, about 7pt in the feed.
3. Too much gold, counted by touches rather than area. Each phone card carries five or six butter touches (dot, underline, button, pathway, glow, logo), against our own one gold detail rule. Ad 02 is about two thirds butter, and the butter button measures only 1.57 to 1 against cream.
4. Things that read as templated or AI: the glossy 3D Orbit in the same spot on four cards, the sheen and glow, the 9:41 clock, and callouts that repeat or cover the screen.
5. Copy that breaks our gates. The stage check screen in 03 says "a safe, capable 16" and "the screen battle", and "Five more minutes?" is now a phrase Kairoo and Ohana use.

What will make it win:
- Lead on the script: "Say this" against "Not this" for one named 8 to 13 moment. Exact words for one moment is the unit that grew Good Inside without paid media, and it already has a working share path (/say/<id>).
- Use the star quest as the conversion ad, because no competitor has it.
- Go mostly cream and ink, with one butter mark.
- Carry the hook word for word on every post.

Honest limits:
- The Meta Ad Library was blocked from here, so no competitor ad is shown to be a proven winner by days live.
- "The script is what gets shared" is an inference from the product as built and from similar cases. Today it cannot be measured, because /say/ hands strangers to a bare /starter-pack with no source code. It must not be reported to Justin as tested.
- Nothing here guarantees results. The organic test (ad studio Phase 5) decides, and only a proven post gets money.

Disagreements settled in earlier rounds:
(a) "Five more minutes?": retire the hook, keep the format. In order of weight: Kairoo and Ohana now use the phrase; it belongs to the little ones' bedtime, not 8 to 13 gaming; and the card's one question should be the fixed CTA. The question hook data is only a weak signal. 8% of 523 long running Meta ads opened with a question, but the source gives no base rate.
(b) Hook test or format variety: Round 1 varies only the hook on one held treatment, as the ad studio skill requires. Format variety comes in Round 2 and at boost time, because the claim that Meta rewards distinct creatives is vendor sourced and only matters once money is spent.
(c) Mumsnet words: paraphrase in ads. Exact quotes go only in organic posts under A THING PARENTS SAY, because paid use of an anonymous poster's words raises consent.
(d) The night problem: 'The phone is in their room all night' is a 13 to 15 script, so it is replaced by 'The Year 6 phone plan, before the box is opened' (migration 261, builder, free).
(e) Ad 01 and concept 1 share one headline: "They cannot stop in the middle of a match."

Objections settled in this round (all accepted; reasons are in the relevant fields):
(f) Measurement. /v/stage-share counts stage result shares only. Script shares stay unmeasured until /say/ carries a source code through to /starter-pack. Each variant gets an Instagram code and a Facebook code. The Instagram bio link is swapped to the live variant's code on the day it posts. Raw starts are reported beside the rate, and a lead of one or two starts counts as a tie.
(g) Motion figures corrected. Hit rates are published for five formats, not nine. The multipliers are a "spend use ratio", and Celebrity tops that list at 2.1x.
(h) Snapchat evidence. Both Mumsnet threads are about 13 year olds, while the script is written for 8 to 10. The parent quotes are now labelled as such, the under 13 case rests on Ofcom figures marked unverified (the chart pack PDF returned 403 from here too), and rank 3 drops to medium confidence.
(i) Crop rule. On /say/ the situation paragraph sits between the title and SAY THIS (PublicScriptView.tsx, checked), so a script crop is one continuous run from the sheet's top ink edge down through NOT THIS, with nothing removed from the middle.
(j) Rank 5. Free words exist only for a parent who has not handed over the phone yet. The bedtime scripts for 11 to 13 are paid, so no ad offers words for a phone that is already in the bedroom. The 'Phone to bed, unasked' mission is added as in product proof.
(k) Screen size. A fixed screen slot of at most 30% of the card is used on all five Round 1 cards. At full width, the jobs first card measured about 10.2% butter and broke our own limit.
(l) Presentation. Round 1 uses flat crops with no phone frame, so there is no composited cream status bar over the espresso /say/ page. The phone frame returns only as a Round 2 format.
(m) Concept 4's sub now says "Bedtime no stars can buy." The old "Some times" read as "Sometimes". Bedtime is a real default window (defaultBedtimeFor and checkProtectedWindow in lib/quests/time-tiers.ts).
(n) Concept 2's underline moves from "Snapchat" to "They are not", so our mark never sits under another brand's yellow.

What Justin needs to do:
1. Decide on changing the stage check wording ("a safe, capable 16", "the screen battle").
2. Confirm the named scripts are live and free in production.
3. Decide whether to make 'When Group Chat Drama Comes Home' free, and whether to make 'They cannot sleep because of their phone' free (both are paid in source).
4. Take one real evening photo of his own hand holding his phone.
5. Send Ad Library screenshots, with "Started running on" visible, for Kairoo, Balance Phone, Qustodio, Good Inside and Greenlight.
6. When posting, swap the Instagram bio link to each variant's own code on the day it goes up.

winning_patterns.pattern: Exact words for one named moment. Short pieces that give a parent the precise thing to say grew the biggest parenting brand in this space without paid media.
winning_patterns.evidence: Fortune (Feb and Mar 2026): 3.4m Instagram followers, $34m revenue, and a business that 'grew organically out of the positive response she received on Instagram'. New York magazine describes role play with 'specific things for parents to say'. No paid Meta evidence was found. That this format drove the growth is the reporters' reading plus our inference. Medium confidence.
winning_patterns.who_uses_it: Good Inside (Dr Becky). Kairoo now offers 'a conversation script' from its quiz.

winning_patterns.pattern: A real person to camera, cut with a screen recording, in many short versions of one idea
winning_patterns.evidence: Motion ad library: Bark has 148 active ads and adds about 9 a week. All 20 of those shown are video, 17 to 59 seconds long, mostly a parent or creator to camera plus a screen recording, with up to 6 versions of one idea. Days live are not shown, so this is what Bark tests, not proven winners. The 2021 SocialPeta snapshot had 41% image. Medium confidence.
winning_patterns.who_uses_it: Bark. Our version can only be Justin or a consenting real family member, never a synthetic parent.

winning_patterns.pattern: Spread through parent WhatsApp groups and organic release, not paid media
winning_patterns.evidence: Thousands joined a WhatsApp group from an Instagram invite within 24 hours (ITV, Feb 2024). The US PSA 'Let's Change The Norm' was released organically and drew over 13 million views (GlobeNewswire, Sept 2025), using recognition through irony. High confidence for the facts.

winning_patterns.pattern: A quiz funnel whose ad says plainly what you get from the quiz
winning_patterns.evidence: TheNextWeb 2020 case: an ad stating what users would learn had 80% higher CTR and 40% lower CPC. Vendor funnel rates are about 71% from view to start and 66% from start to finish (Interact). Low to medium confidence; one case.
winning_patterns.who_uses_it: Kairoo ('5-minute quiz' giving three things to try, a script and checkpoints). Balance Phone (a readiness quiz in its Instagram ad of 14 Oct, not on its homepage).

winning_patterns.pattern: Plain, native, low fi creative over polish; demo formats hit often
winning_patterns.evidence: Motion 2026 benchmark (578,750 creatives, $1.29bn spend, all verticals). Hit rates are published for only five formats: Unboxing 9.8%, Offer-First Banner 8.6%, Demo 8.1%, Testimonial 6.5%, Celebrity 5.9%. Its spend use ratio is a format's share of spend divided by its share of creative volume. On that ratio, Letter is about 1.7x, Unconventional Text Placement about 1.5x and Post It about 1.3x, but Celebrity tops the list at 2.1x, so this is not a clean low fi win. Segwise, on 523 surviving Meta ads: clarity, not polish, is the common factor. Barry Hott (practitioner): 'Pretty ads stand out and get skipped.' Medium confidence for the direction, low for the sizes.
winning_patterns.who_uses_it: Nuet ('It reads the school emails. You stop missing things.', logged in competitor-sightings.md)

winning_patterns.pattern: Pain point statements are the commonest opener among long running ads; question openers are rare among them
winning_patterns.evidence: Of 523 Meta ads still running after 30 days, pain point, authority and pattern interrupt hooks made up 71%, and only 8% opened with a question (Segwise citing Brandsearch; method not disclosed). The source gives no base rate for how many ads open with a question, so this is a weak signal, not a measured survival rate. Our CTA pill is already the card's one question.
winning_patterns.who_uses_it: Bark ('I wasn't going to post this, but other parents need to hear it.'). Kairoo ('Stop being the screen-time bad cop.')

winning_patterns.pattern: One long running practical message about earning: chores in, reward out
winning_patterns.evidence: Greenlight's chores message has run from its 2020 TV spot onward, and a 2021 SocialPeta teardown named a chores led creative a top performer. Running for years is a weak sign it works, and the performance claim is dated. Medium confidence.
winning_patterns.who_uses_it: Greenlight, GoHenry, and Kairoo's banked minutes. None ties earning to screen time with protected time no stars can buy, which is our star quest.

winning_patterns.pattern: Looking AI made costs attention and trust
winning_patterns.evidence: NIQ (Dec 2024, 2,000+ viewers, EEG on about 150): viewers spotted most AI ads, rated them more annoying, boring and confusing, remembered them less, and showed a negative halo on the brand. Getty VisualGPS: most people want AI images disclosed, and Europeans are the most sceptical. McDonald's NL pulled its AI Christmas ad in Dec 2025. High confidence for the finding; applying it to our Orbit render is inference.
winning_patterns.who_uses_it: A pattern to avoid. GoHenry's 2026 AI aged up child is the nearest competitor example and would break our no synthetic person rule.

winning_patterns.pattern: Visibly different creatives rather than reworded copies of one template, once money is spent
winning_patterns.evidence: Jon Loomer and Excite Media on Meta Andromeda. Meta is quoted calling creative diversification 'the most effective lever'. The similarity thresholds and the '70% different' rule are agency figures and unverified. Low to medium confidence; relevant only at boost.

winning_patterns.pattern: Proof by borrowed numbers: user counts, star ratings, press logos, risk reversal. Listed so that we do NOT copy it.
winning_patterns.evidence: Ohana: '100.000+ parents trust Ohana'. Balance Phone: 'Rated 4.8/5', 'over 30,000 happy subscribers', a press strip and a 14 day refund. Qustodio: 'over 6 million parents'. Bark: 'award-winning'. All fetched 19 Oct 2026. Our gates forbid each one we cannot evidence; our proof is the real screen.

viral_feature.feature: The script: one named moment set as 'Say this' against 'Not this', free on a public /say/<id> page that a parent forwards to their school WhatsApp group. The share hook is the moment for this age: 'They cannot stop in the middle of a match.' The star quest is the reason to buy, not the thing people forward.
viral_feature.why: All three agents agreed, for four reasons. (1) It is the same unit that grew Good Inside organically: the exact words for one moment. (2) 'Not this' is the line a parent recognises themselves in ('It is a game. Turn it off now or it goes in the bin.'), the same recognition device as SFC's 13 million view PSA. (3) UK parents demonstrably spread this topic through school WhatsApp groups (SFC). (4) It is useful tonight and can be forwarded without anyone signing up. The star quest is our strongest difference from competitors, but a screenshot of a child's quest page has less pass it on value than a sentence another parent can use tonight. So the star quest is the conversion ad, not the share hook. This is INFERENCE from the product as built plus similar cases. It is not our own share data, it is currently unmeasurable, and it must not be reported to Justin as tested.
viral_feature.proof:
The share path exists. components/scripts/ShareScript.tsx sends /say/<uuid> with the words in the message. app/say/[id]/opengraph-image.tsx sets the quote at 60px, so it reads in a WhatsApp preview without a tap, and carries no referral code. app/say/[id]/page.tsx serves any script by id with no sign in.

Free scripts that fit 8 to 13 (is_free true in the migration files; production unconfirmed): 'They cannot stop in the middle of a match' (migration 186, builder), 'The Year 6 phone plan, before the box is opened' (migration 261, builder), 'The no confiscation promise, said out loud' (migration 261, explorer) and 'Everyone is on Snapchat and they are not' (migration 180, builder). Not for this audience: 'The phone is in their room all night' (migration 186) is free but Shaper, ages 13 to 15.

MEASUREMENT GAP. /v/stage-share (migration 379) counts shares of the stage check RESULT only (components/starter/ShareStage.tsx, lib/share/stage.ts). It does not count script shares. For a stranger, the /say/ page's sticky button links to a bare /starter-pack with no ?src (components/scripts/PublicScriptView.tsx line 224). So every stage check that starts from a forwarded script is counted as untagged.

What turns this claim into evidence: a source code on /say/ shares, carried through to /starter-pack. It is a small build, raised with the review board first, not assumed.

palette.role: Palette A background: the default, and the only background in Round 1. Its edge against Instagram's white light mode feed is only 1.06 to 1, so Round 2 and any boosted set add ink cards.

The proof: a real app capture at 390 wide x3, cropped as one continuous run and never redrawn or edited. It sits in one fixed screen slot at or under 30% of the card's area. Script cards use the public /say/<id> page only. Its butter header band reads 'A script from Guided Childhood · Ages 8 to 10' and counts in the butter check.
palette.share: at or under 30% (15 to 20% on Palette B)

palette.role: Headline colour on cream, and the edge drawn around a flat crop that has no edge of its own (2.5px, the same as the /say/ sheet). Also the Palette B background, which none of the competitors checked uses (Kairoo, Qustodio, Bark, Balance Phone).
palette.share: about 10% on Palette A; about 65% as the Palette B background

palette.role: The default CTA button, exactly as shared/tokens.css defines .btn-ink: espresso background, white #FFFFFF text, box-shadow 0 5px 0 #171307. It matches the starter pack button the parent taps next. Espresso on cream is 13.81 to 1; white on espresso is 14.66 to 1.
The sub line and the hook line 'Three questions, no sign up.' on cream only (7.13 to 1). Never on the ink background, where it measures 2.25 to 1.

ONE mark per card: the underline under the moment words on cream, OR the CTA button on ink (ink text on butter is 10.21 to 1), never both. Plus the logo mark. Never a background, never text, and never under a third party brand name.
palette.share: under 3% added by design, plus about 1% for the logo; total butter including the real screen at or under 10%

palette.role: Only as the shadow of the butter underline or the butter button. Never text: it is 2.43 to 1 on cream, which fails AA.
On Palette B every line of text (headline, sub, hook line) is cream, at 16.07 to 1. A stepped down hook line uses cream at reduced opacity, never ink soft.

creative_direction.gold_rule:
Butter (#EDC35F) is a single mark, never a surface. On a paid ad:
(1) It is never the background, so the butter background is retired for ads. It made 02 about two thirds butter.
(2) It is never text.
(3) Design adds exactly one butter touch per card: the underline on cream or the button on ink, never both, plus the logo mark.
(4) On cream, the underline always sits under the moment words of the headline, three words or fewer, the same way on every card, so it never becomes a second variable. It never sits under another brand's name. 'Snapchat' has its own yellow, so concept 2 underlines 'They are not'.
(5) Total butter on the finished card, including what is inside the real screen (the /say/ header band, the butter in the My time card), stays at or under 10% of the area. It is checked with the pixel script before a card goes in a pack.

The fixed screen slot of at most 30% is what keeps the jobs first card inside that limit. Its My time crop is 17.5% butter on its own: at full width the card measured about 10.2%, and at about 760 wide about 7.7%.

Why: the 'too much gold' feeling comes from five or six butter touches per card, not from area (5 to 9%). That breaks brand/GDC_SOCIAL_VISUAL_SYSTEM.md section 7 ('One gold detail per card'). A butter button on cream is only 1.57 to 1, so the espresso button reads better. Kairoo uses a near identical amber (#E9C46A) with Nunito on near cream, so butter only stays distinctive as one consistent device, the underline stroke (Ehrenberg-Bass distinctive assets). The palette rests on contrast and difference from competitors. No credible UK parent colour benchmark exists, so no claim is made about which colours parents 'trust'.
not_ai_rules: No 3D character render on a cold paid ad to parents. Orbit and the Planet Friends stay for organic and child facing work. Whether the render reads as AI to UK parents is untested, but it sits in the same spot on four cards, and NIQ found that AI looking ads cost attention and trust.

Round 1 uses no phone frame. Each real screen is shown as a flat crop. A /say/ script is cropped at the sheet's own 2.5px ink edge, so no espresso page margin and no dark drop shadow show on the cream card. An app crop with no edge of its own gets the same 2.5px ink edge drawn by the template OUTSIDE the capture. This is how the parent meets the script on /say/, and it removes the composited look (a cream status bar over a dark web page). The phone frame returns only as a Round 2 format. There, its status bar colour and ink are set to whatever really sits at the top of that capture, never the default cream.

brief.test_plan:
Follow ad-studio Phase 5. Nothing is paid until a post has proved itself organically.

BEFORE ANYTHING POSTS (Justin):
(1) Confirm that 'They cannot stop in the middle of a match', 'Everyone is on Snapchat and they are not' and 'The Year 6 phone plan, before the box is opened' are live and is_free in the production scripts table. Only the migration files were read, and later migrations such as 371 may have rewritten them.
(2) Decide whether to change the stage check wording ('a safe, capable 16', 'the screen battle').
(3) Make the template changes. Render ONE card in the stacked layout with the fixed screen slot, and check two things: that the headline holds 3 lines at 88 to 96px and everything sits inside the safe area, and that a continuous script crop (header through NOT THIS) is readable at feed size. If it is not, end all three script crops after SAY THIS, as the not-AI rules say. Then render the round.
(4) Every card must pass the Phase 4 gates, the butter area check (the jobs first card especially) and npm run ai-tells.
(5) Before concept 2's evidence goes into any document, verify the Ofcom under 13 Snapchat figures against the chart pack. The ad copy itself quotes no figure.

ROUND 1, testing the hook. The held treatment: stacked layout, cream, the fixed screen slot at or under 30% with a flat crop and no phone frame, the espresso button, the butter underline under the moment words, no callouts, and the hook line. Five variants:
- 04 tell-digi rebuilt (the control)
- concept 1, Mid match
- concept 2, Left out of the plans
- concept 3, Before the box is opened
- concept 4, Jobs first

LINKS. On the founder links page (/dashboard/admin/videos), make TWO codes per variant, one with channel Instagram and one with channel Facebook. That is ten codes in all. Log both codes for each variant in content/ads/results-log.md.

POSTING. Justin posts each variant as an ordinary post on the family Instagram and Facebook, one variant at a time, on the same weekday and in the same time slot, one week apart, so the day does not decide the winner. That stretches Round 1 to about five weeks; it is a design guard, not sourced data.
- On the day a variant posts, set the Instagram bio link to that variant's Instagram code, and leave it there for its full seven days. The post says 'link in bio'. Without the swap, every Instagram start lands on one code and the test cannot be read.
- On Facebook, put the variant's Facebook code in the body.
- Give each post seven days.

JUDGING. Judge on stage checks begun per thousand reached, and on signups. Never judge on likes or views. Read Instagram and Facebook separately, then together.
- A winner needs at least 300 reached; below that it is too early.
- Always report the raw number of stage checks begun beside the rate. If the leader is ahead by only one or two starts, call it a tie and too early, and re-post both rather than boosting. This is a design guard against small numbers, not a sourced threshold. content/ads/results-log.md shows nothing has run yet, so there is no base rate to judge small differences against.

ROUND 2, testing the format, on the Round 1 winning moment:
- the phone card (the phone frame, with its status bar matched to the capture)
- the plain text ink card (concept 5)
- the carousel (concept 6)
- the real hand photo (concept 7)
- the 15 second stage check recording (concept 8), once the copy is fixed
Cream and ink cards are mixed from here on, and 03-the-quiz-our-way joins here. This builds the visibly distinct set that vendor sources say Meta's delivery rewards when money is spent. Use the same per channel codes and the same bio link swap.

SHARE MEASURE. /v/stage-share (migration 379) measures shares of the stage check RESULT only. Comparing it with ad link starts tells us how often the result gets shared, nothing more. Script shares are unmeasured until /say/ carries a source code through to /starter-pack. Today the /say/ sticky button links to a bare /starter-pack (components/scripts/PublicScriptView.tsx line 224), and ShareScript carries no code by design. Until then, the script as the viral unit is inference and must not be reported to Justin as tested. Raise the per script source code build with the review board as the thing that turns this claim into evidence.

THEN, only for a proven winner: a one block boost brief for Justin, naming the post, the audience (UK parents of children 8 to 13), the skill's small daily budget and a fixed end date.
- The brief states plainly that the organic winner was proven with people who already follow us, not a cold audience. The small budget and fixed end date cap what a cold flop can cost.
- Run 3 to 5 visibly distinct creatives of that one idea, not reworded copies.
- Vendor data says winners fatigue after about 4 to 8 weeks (Marpipe 2025, low to medium confidence), so plan the next moment before then.

LOG every variant in content/ads/results-log.md: date, round, hook, format, Instagram code, Facebook code, posting day and slot, the date of the bio link swap, reached, raw stage checks begun, rate per thousand, signups, verdict, and one line learned.

research.name: Ad performance researcher
research.summary: Ad performance researcher, council lane: what actually performs. I looked at all nine current ads. Repo files read: THE-STORY 1, 2, 9 and 10, ad-studio SKILL.md, competitor-sightings.md, results-log.md (nothing has run yet), ShareScript.tsx, ShareStage.tsx, lib/share/stage.ts, app/say/[id], and the scripts migrations. The Meta Ad Library was blocked, so I can't evidence days live for any competitor ad. The only competitor with a real live creative inventory I could reach is Bark, through Motion's public ad library: 148 active ads, about 9 new creatives a week, and every one of the 20 shown is a video, mostly a parent talking to camera cut with a screen recording, 17 to 59 seconds long. For the other brands the evidence is their own sites, app stores, TV spot archives and trade press, and none of it says which Facebook or Instagram ads run longest. Two findings change our creative straight away. First, Kairoo's site now leads on '5 more minutes', calling it 'the phrase that starts the nightly battle', and Ohana's App Store page has a '5 more minutes please' feature, so our flat card 'Five more minutes?' walks into a phrase two competitors already use. Second, three of the four new phone ads have a fixable fault: 01 shows a Shaper (13 to 15) teen script to parents of 8 to 13 year olds; 03 shows a real screen with 'a safe, capable 16' (gate 5) and 'the screen battle', and its subline swaps the hook for 'No sign up. Two minutes.'; 04 carries no 'Three questions, no sign up.' line. Cross-format benchmarks from 2025 and 2026 are mostly vendor data. They point to: native, plain and clear beats polished; demo and testimonial formats win often; question hooks survive least; video is preferred for cold traffic, but statics are still most of what accounts run; Meta now rewards creative that looks visibly different, not reworded copies of one template. My answer on virality, with the reasoning: the part of our service most likely to be shared is the script, a 'Say this / Not this' pair for one named moment. It is practical, gives a parent words they can use tonight, and already has a working share path that fits how UK parents pass things on (WhatsApp groups). The star quest is our strongest reason to buy, because no competitor has it, but it's less likely to be forwarded on its own.
recommendations: Retire the 'Five more minutes?' hook (flat card 01-one-moment). Kairoo now calls '5 more minutes' the phrase that starts the nightly battle, and Ohana uses '5 more minutes please' as a feature. Lead on the answer instead, for example 'They cannot stop in the middle of a match.' with our Say this.

Make the script the lead creative and the share hook: a large crop of the real script screen showing Say this and Not this, one named 8 to 13 moment per variant. Use the free scripts 'They cannot stop in the middle of a match', 'The Year 6 phone plan, before the box is opened' and 'The no confiscation promise, said out loud'. Each has a public /say/ page that proves the claim with no paywall. This is the Motion 'Letter' or text-heavy native structure, using our own real screen.

Fix three of the four phone ads before anything is posted. In 01, swap the Shaper (13 to 15) footprint script for one of the 8 to 13 scripts above. In 03, recapture the stage check screen (or fix the source copy) so it no longer says 'a safe, capable 16' or 'the screen battle you are facing'; until then, do not use it. In 03 and 04, make the line under the button 'Three questions, no sign up.' word for word.

Cut the gold to one accent per card: the CTA or the underline, not the background. Turn 02 jobs-first from a full butter background to cream, with butter only on the button. That serves Justin's 'not too much gold' and gives Meta visibly different creatives.

Diversify by format, not by headline. Meta's delivery rewards visually distinct creatives, so the test set should be 3 to 5 genuinely different structures: (a) the script screen crop, static; (b) the star quest real screen, static, as the conversion ad; (c) a 15 second screen recording of the stage check end to end (the product shorts skill; THE-STORY says it is showable in fifteen seconds); (d) Justin to camera reading one script in one take, a real person in Bark's dominant format with no synthetic parent; (e) a two slide carousel, Not this then Say this.

Prefer statement hooks over question hooks in the headline. The thin evidence says question hooks survive least, and our CTA is already a question. Name one moment, then stop (the Nuet lesson already logged).

Say in the ad what the parent gets from the quiz ('your child's stage, and the words for tonight'). An ad that states what you will learn from a quiz drew far more clicks in the only case found, and it separates us from Balance Phone's ready or not ready.
Change the flat cards' 'AGES 4 TO 16' corner label to the band the ad targets (8 to 13) when the ad is aimed at the first phone years.

Borrow Bark's comment to get the link mechanic only as an organic test, and only if a compliant auto reply exists (for example comment STAGE). Otherwise keep 'link in bio' as the ad-studio skill says. This is an inference, not evidenced for our audience.

Do not borrow user counts, star ratings, press logo strips, an AI aged child, an 'award-winning' claim or fear framing. These are the proof devices of Ohana, Balance, Qustodio, GoHenry and Bark, and our gates forbid each one we cannot evidence. Our proof is the real screen.

Before the next round, ask Justin for Ad Library screenshots with 'Started running on' showing, for Kairoo, Balance Phone, Qustodio, Good Inside and Greenlight. No days live evidence was reachable from here, so nothing above ranks a competitor ad as proven.

Measure what gets shared, not just clicks: compare /v/stage-share starts against ad link starts on the founder links page. If scripts are the viral unit, a per-script source code on /say/ shares would prove it. This needs a small build, and it should be raised with the board first, not assumed.

research.name: Parent problems researcher
research.summary:
Parent problems lane. I ranked the ten problems that UK parents of 8 to 13 year olds raise most often and most painfully. The sources are Mumsnet threads I fetched today (19 October 2026), UK surveys, and Qustodio's Trustpilot page. I built on the repo's two earlier sweeps rather than redoing them: research/homepage-audience-language.md (8 August) and content/packs/2026-10-09-digi-shorts/top-problems.md (9 October; 330 coded Reddit posts and 51 Mumsnet threads). Reddit and Netmums are blocked from this environment, both for search and for fetch. Every Reddit or Netmums figure below therefore comes from the 9 October file and is labelled that way. I did not re-verify it. Mumsnet thread pages could be fetched, so those quotes are word for word with dates and reply counts.

The ranking, by frequency and intensity: (1) the switch off fight and gaming rage, (2) whether to give a first phone, with the fear of the child being left out, (3) pressure to join Snapchat or TikTok under 13, (4) unkind group chats, (5) the phone in the bedroom at night, (6) parental controls that fail or get got round, (7) finding porn or disturbing content and not knowing what to say, (8) feeling like the bad guy and a failing parent, (9) another adult undoing the rules, (10) "addicted", where nothing else interests them. Six of the ten have a real screen or a script that already answers them.

The newest and most intense evidence is a Mumsnet thread from 15 October 2026 with 147 replies: a parent whose child got past iPhone parental controls through proxies to reach adult content. It is live proof that blocking alone fails, which is the gap we sell into. Our product cannot honestly answer number 10, and only partly answers number 9.

What this means for the ads: the current set mostly covers problems 2, 8 and a general DiGi message. None covers the most intense problems for 8 to 13s, which are mid match gaming rage, Snapchat pressure, group chats and the phone at night. Ad 01 lifts out a teenager's online footprint script, a poor fit for parents of 8 to 13s. Ad 03's real screen says "the screen battle" and "a safe, capable 16", and its line under the button is "No sign up. Two minutes." rather than the hook word for word.
recommendations: Build the next ad round around problems 1, 3, 4 and 5, the most intense for 8 to 13s and so far unadvertised. Each one already has a real script to put in the phone mockup: 'They cannot stop in the middle of a match' (migration 186), 'Everyone is on Snapchat and they are not' (migration 180), 'When Group Chat Drama Comes Home' (migration 151) and 'The phone is in their room all night' (migration 186). Capture each as a real screen in content/ads/screens/ and lift the 'say this' line out as the callout.

Use parents' words for the moment as the hook, never a quote presented as testimony. Usable framings: 'They cannot stop mid match.', 'Everyone is on Snapchat. They are not.', 'The class chat at eleven at night.', 'I don't want a knee jerk no.' Any Mumsnet line used word for word must carry the A THING PARENTS SAY eyebrow. Use it organically with a link, or paraphrase it; paid use of an anonymous poster's exact words raises the consent question the 9 October report flagged.

Swap ad 01's callout from the teenager's online footprint script to a script for this age (the mid match one is the strongest fit). Keep the 'Know what to say before the argument' headline, which rank 1 and rank 7 both support.

Fix ad 03 before it runs. The real stage check screen says 'the screen battle' and 'a safe, capable 16' (gate 5 and competitor lesson 3). Change the live copy, then recapture, rather than editing the image. Make the line under the button the hook word for word: 'What stage is your child? Three questions, no sign up.' Add the same line under ad 02's button.

Use the 15 October 2026 Mumsnet thread on controls bypassed through proxies (147 replies) as the evidence behind a 'we are not parental controls' angle: the controls held until they did not, and what is left is what the child understands. Never claim we block anything, and never use porn or harm as the visual or the hook.
Do not run any ad on problem 10 ('addicted', cutting screen time down) or claim less screen time. Do not imply a second parent account (problem 9). Neither has an honest proof path today.

Before any boost, have Justin confirm the scripts named above are live and free in the production scripts table. Later migrations such as 371 may have rewritten them, and I only read the migration files.

research.name: Creative director
research.summary:
Creative director's verdict: the current ads are clean and use real app screens, which is the hardest thing to get right, and none of them is AI made in the way Justin fears. But they will not beat the competitors as they stand, for five fixable reasons:

1. The gold is overdone. Gold covers only 3 to 9 percent of each phone card by area, but every card has five separate gold touches: the eyebrow dot, the underline, the button, the pathway ribbon and the logo. Our own visual system allows one. The yellow card, 02-jobs-first, is 66 percent gold.
2. The gold button does not stand out. It measures 1.57 to 1 against the cream background and 1.37 to 1 against the blue one, below the 3 to 1 accessibility minimum for buttons.
3. The hook is cut in half. "Three questions, no sign up." appears word for word on only 2 of 9 cards, and on those it is set at about 7pt in the feed, the smallest text on the card.
4. Three things make the cards look templated rather than human. The glossy 3D Orbit character, likely the most AI looking element though nobody has tested it with parents, sits in the same place on all four flat cards. Lifted callouts repeat text that is already on the screen. On 04 a callout covers the screen copy so the screen looks broken.
5. Our colours are not ours alone. Kairoo, the closest competitor, uses Nunito in its app with an amber (#E9C46A) nearly identical to our gold (#EDC35F), on a near cream background (#FBF6EF). Of the four competitors whose sites we checked, none uses a dark ink background, so that is the open space.

Recommended palette: mostly cream and ink, gold kept to one mark.
- Cream #F9F8F6 for about 55 percent of the card
- The real screen for about 25 to 30 percent
- Ink #1A1A2E for the headline and an ink button, about 12 percent
- Ink soft #52526A for the sub line, about 3 percent
- Gold #EDC35F for one underline stroke only, under 3 percent, plus the logo mark at about 1 percent
- One variant on a dark ink background, with gold used only as the button, where it reaches 10.2 to 1

Gold rule: gold is never the background, never text, and only one gold touch is added per card. Total gold, including what is on the screen itself, stays at or under 10 percent of the card.

Verdicts on the 9 cards: change 01, 02, 03 and 04 (phone), Five more minutes and Not a verdict (rebuild them without Orbit), and turn 14 Oct C into a plain text control. Drop 02-real-screen and 14 Oct A.

Separately for Justin: the stage check screen itself says "a safe, capable 16" and "the screen battle", which breaks our own ad rules. That is a change to the product's wording, so it is his call.

Evidence quality: the case for authenticity is strong (NIQ, Getty, the McDonald's NL pull). The case for text size is moderate, from a print eye tracking study. The claim that Meta's Andromeda groups similar looking ads together comes only from agency and vendor blogs. We found no credible public research on which colours UK parents respond to in feed ads, and general colour psychology is weak evidence, so the palette rests on contrast, being different from competitors, and our own tokens. Measurements and the thumbnail sheets are in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-guided-childhood/912fb4b8-ae4c-536b-bb44-27b66a5ad0ab/scratchpad/cd/ (measure.py, thumb.png, feed.png).
recommendations: PALETTE A, the default for most variants (tokens only): cream #F9F8F6 background, about 55%. The real screen, about 25 to 30% (pick screens that are not mostly gold). Ink #1A1A2E for the headline and the CTA button, about 12%. Ink soft #52526A for the sub line and hook line, about 3%. Gold #EDC35F as ONE underline stroke under 3 words or fewer, under 3%, with gold dark #C99A28 only as that stroke's shadow. The logo mark stays as the brand mark, about 1%.
